blocks.text: *How your abilities work, and where they come from.*
Mastery points buy your skills

In Unwritten, **your skills come from fighting with a kind of weapon.** Fight with a sword and Sword Mastery grows: two thirds of the experience every kill gives you also goes to the mastery of the weapon in your hands, faster with a better weapon. **Every Sword Mastery level gives you one Mastery Point for the sword**, and you spend it in the Skills window (**K**): press **+** on a skill, and the first point **learns** it, each point after that raises it one level. What you learn is yours for good. The window also shows how much experience the next mastery level needs. There are no classes — the skills you chose are what define you, and what you are holding decides which of them you may use right now.
Every weapon type has its own pool

Each weapon *type* has its own **pool of skills** — **3 ultimates** plus a set of normal skills. You do not find them and no weapon carries them: every skill names the **mastery level** in its weapon at which you can buy it, and some name a skill that needs **at least one point** first — only when the skill really uses that other one (its stacks, its pile, its cast, or a moment it causes). The Skills window draws a weapon as a line from mastery **0** to **70**: each skill sits where it opens, a skill and the ones that need it share a row joined by lines, a skill still out of reach is faint, one you can buy is grey, and one you have bought wears the weapon's colour.

**Your ultimates point at your build.** Each weapon's three ultimates steer toward a different playstyle — and toward which Ring stats to invest in — and they sit deep enough in the mastery that reaching one is a statement about how you have been fighting.
Styles, forms and calling them out

Every weapon fights in a **style**, and each of its skills is one numbered **form** of that style, counted in the order the weapon teaches them — the sword's style is **Blossom Wind**, and its first form is **Piercing Gust**. A skill's card says which form it is.

Every skill you use is called out over your head and in the chat, every time it fires — by its name alone, *"Last Petal!!"*. A passive stays silent unless it is efficient. **Efficiency** is a critical hit for a whole skill: each time a trademark skill fires it has a **5%** chance to be efficient, whatever weapon you hold, and then every number it puts out that time is raised by a further **+20%** and you make the full call — *"Blossom Wind style, 21st form, Thousand Petals!!"*. Every trademark skill can be efficient, ultimates included; a skill that is not a trademark skill has no number to raise and never is. The shadows call out their skills the same way. You can hide other players' calls under **Settings ▸ Gameplay**.

**You cannot have everything.** A weapon's mastery stops at **70**, so you get at most 70 points for it — and the sword's skills can take **129** levels between them. So two people holding the same sword need not play alike at all: they have the skills they each chose. Every skill in a weapon's pool reinforces that weapon's identity, so however far you take it, it still plays like that weapon.
Skill levels, your Ring and your weapon power them

Three things make a skill strong. **Your Ring stats scale it** (see *Stats & the Ring*) — a heal only pays off if you invested MP, a damage skill only hits hard if you invested Attack or Magic Attack. **Its level** — every level after the first adds **+5%**: level 1 is the skill as it comes, level 5 is **+20%**, level 10 is **+45%**. Actives, passives and ultimates all grow the same way, but only while their weapon is in your hands; a potion gets none. A skill goes up to level **10** when what grows is mostly damage, **5** when it is a defensive or utility percentage or a number of charges, and stays at **1** when nothing on it grows. The weapon in your hands decides how many of those levels count: a 10-level skill counts **2** of them with a Raw weapon, then 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, and all **10** at A; a 5-level skill counts 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 5. Levels you bought are never lost. And **a forged weapon's trademark** raises one skill of its type by **+5%** to **+20%**, by its grade (see *Weapons*).

A skill's level and a trademark raise its **main numbers** — every one of them, on every effect: the damage it deals, the heal, the shield, the damage an ailment ticks for, how big a buff or debuff is, and how many stacks it adds. A skill with a strike and a damage buff has both raised. They never raise a chance, a duration or the number of hits — only your Ring moves those. A skill's card says **PASSIVE**, **ACTIVE** or **ULTIMATE** beside its name, lists what it requires (green when you have it, red when you don't), shows **Skill level N / max**, and gives every growing number now and at the next level — what an ordinary cast lands, with your Ring and the trademark of the weapon you hold already counted in; for a weapon you are not holding it counts every level you bought. The trademark bonus also gets its own line under each effect.
What a skill is made of
Every skill combines two things:

items: **Its numbers** — how much damage, how many hits, how long it lasts, its mana cost, cooldown, cast time, range, and area.
**Its effects** — what it actually *does*.

blocks.text: Active and passive skills
Most skills are **active**: they take a hotbar slot, and you press them. They cost mana and use the cooldown, cast time, range, and area above.

Some are **passive**. A passive takes **no hotbar slot and is never pressed** — it works on its own from the moment you spend a point on it, as long as its weapon is in your hands: it waits for a specific moment in the fight and fires. The small squares above your hotbar show every passive running. The moment it waits for is part of the skill:

items: **After you finish casting a particular skill** — uninterrupted. This is how one skill rides another: Crossed Branches off Piercing Gust, Deep Roots off Still Air.
**When a basic attack of yours lands.** Rising Breeze and Tailwind ride this one.
**When you begin a basic attack.**
**When a hit of yours deals damage.**
**When you kill something.** Second Bloom rides this one.
**When you drop to low health.**
**When you take damage.**
**When you successfully parry.** Parting Clouds rides this one.

blocks.text: A passive **fires as a full skill** — the same visuals and the same effects an active would play. Only the trigger is different. It aims itself, too: a skill that needs a target lands on whatever set it off, and a skill that targets you always lands on you.
What skills can do
Skills are built from a catalog of effects. The common ones:

items: **Damage** — direct harm. A multi-hit strike splits one total across its hits.
**Heal** — restore health now.
**Shield** — raise an absorbing barrier that soaks a set amount of damage, then lapses.

**Raise a stat / lower a stat** — the workhorse. One effect moves one number on the sheet for a while: your damage, attack speed, cast speed, move speed, health or mana regeneration, accuracy, evasion, attack, defense, crit, max health or mana, life steal, mana leech, reflect, or how much damage you take. Everything that used to be a separate Haste, Guard, Regen or Buff is this one effect now.
**Status ailments** — Burn, Poison, and Bleed (damage over time), plus Stun, Freeze, and Silence.
**Parry charges** — each charge erases one incoming hit outright, then is spent.
**Brace charges** — each charge holds back one incoming hit and banks the damage instead; the whole debt lands when the window ends.
**Damage charges** — charges that make your next attacks land harder (or an enemy's land softer). One charge, one attack, spent whether it hits or misses.
**Immunity to being stopped** — a window where nothing flinches, stuns, freezes, silences, shoves or interrupts you.
**Taunt** — force monsters to attack you.
**Knockback / Pull** — shove enemies away or drag them in.
**Cleanse** — strip debuffs off yourself.
**Execute** — bonus damage that grows huge against low-health enemies.
**Dash / Teleport** — close distance in a rush, or blink to a target spot.
**Feed another skill** — add stacks to another skill's pile, or give that pile more time. This is how Second Bloom keeps Thousand Petals going, and how Tailwind feeds Rising Breeze.

blocks.text: **Ultimate skills** are a special tier — the biggest thing a weapon does, at **40 mana** and a long cooldown rather than a charge meter. Every weapon's pool holds **3** of them, and each opens deep into that weapon's mastery: the sword's open at **30**, **45** and **60**.

text: *Status: the skill framework above is in place. Exact numbers, cooldowns, and each weapon's skill pool are still being tuned and drafted.*
